claim: handleInboundEmail writes an inbound attachment's conversation_attachments.order_id from threadOrderId, and threadOrderId is set only from the earliest procurement_conversations row with the message's gmail_thread_id (order created_at asc, then id asc, limit 1), and only when that row's direction, lower-cased, is 'outbound' and its email_headers has no in_reply_to: the order a letter that opened the thread names. Every other case leaves it null. orderId still takes that row's order_id and, when that is null, the 2b fallback (the provider's newest non-terminal order), and orderId still goes to the inbound conversation row, so the reply text keeps the guess (2b text continuity unchanged). confirmDeal now stores in_reply_to and references in the deal confirmation row's email_headers when the row has a Gmail thread id, so a confirmation that opens a new Gmail thread is read as a reply there. Ruling (coordinator, under the founder's 2026-10-07 delegation, not the founder's pick): approving or auto-sending a reply on a guessed order does not make the thread name that order. Before: on origin/main a323cc80b and at 7af3623ef the thread lookup read one row of the thread with no order (any direction); main passed orderId to persistAttachments, so a guessed order reached DocumentIntakeService and was filed as link_method manual, confidence 1; 7af passed that unordered row's order_id, so the second message of a vendor-opened thread could read the first message's inbound row, and a responder draft, staff reply or deal confirmation on the guess could be the row read. With no order on the attachment, intake runs autoLink, which links only an exact order_number in the house (po_number, 0.95). Still open: a reply row stored with no in_reply_to (a deal confirmation written before this change, or a reply to an inbound message that had no Message-ID) that opens a new Gmail thread still names its order there. Static: the verify strips comments outside string literals and checks, in handleInboundEmail, the step-2 block verbatim once; exactly 3 code tokens of threadOrderId (declare, assign, pass: catches ??=, ||=, &&=, destructuring and array writes), 8 of origin and 2 of thread; persistAttachments named once, strings included, and called once with (inserted.id, threadOrderId, ...); no conversation_attachments; the inbound insert with order_id: orderId; the fallback assignment; in persistAttachments its signature, 2 code tokens of orderId and one conversation_attachments insert with order_id: orderId; in confirmDeal the three statements that record the conditional headers; and 9 case names in a-guessed-order-does-not-link-the-paper.spec.ts plus 2 in vendor-doors-are-sealed.spec.ts. Measured 2026-10-07 with bash -c: exit 0 on the branch and on 4 harmless edits (a trailing // comment, a block comment, a URL in a template literal, a URL in a string); exit 1 on 7af3623ef's and a323cc80b's bridge and on each of 26 static mutants; a missing file is a Traceback naming No such file or directory (cannot-run), never exit 0. Spec: 17/17 lane cases and 40/40 vendor-doors cases on the branch; 8 lane cases red with 7af's bridge, 10 with main's; behavioural mutants each turn at least 1 case red except reading the last row instead of the first, which limit(1) makes equivalent and only the static verify catches.
